g.title: tenancy
g.text: amber: control plane · blue: credentials · grey: Postgres truth · green: data plane · red: fail-closed

g.title: cluster_admin
g.text: ADMIN PLANE — the admin key owns everything

g.title: cluster_leader
g.text: TEAM PLANE — a leader key sees ONE enrollment and nothing else

g.title: code
g.text: 32-byte urlsafe · SHA-256 hash only · max_uses · expiry
ONE generic rejection: no expired/exhausted oracle

g.title: enrollment
g.text: hard envelope: budget_tokens / budget_usd per period
team_leader_key_last_used_at → a dead leader is visible

g.title: topup->enrollment
g.text: raises the CAP — the admin's alone

g.title: console
g.text: its own keys · its own usage · its own traces

g.title: ask
g.text: one OPEN ask at a time

g.title: failclosed
g.text: revoked leader key · revoked enrollment (a closed team closes its console)
foreign id → 404, exactly like a missing one

g.title: gate
g.text: per-key allocation + team envelope SUM + shared overflow pool
both gates SUM the same ledger rows with the same fraction weighting
→ the per-key gate and the team cap can never disagree

g.title: ledger
g.text: budgets are SUMs, never a counter

g.title: audit
g.text: actor = the enrollment LABEL — never key material

g.title: teammate
g.text: POST /v1/enroll {code, name} → a personal hllm- key
budgets + MCP grants stamped in the SAME transaction

g.title: legend
g.text: admin (the cap) · team leader (its own team, inside the cap)
hash-only, shown once: enrollment code, leader key, teammate key
a teammate's key is a data-plane credential and nothing more
no credential, no console; no id oracle either
